quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles must use the full lane width like all other vehicles.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle:

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because the chance is small that another vehicle is coming.
By using the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane is next to a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never pass by driving on the shoulder. A solid yellow line means no passing.

questions.question: You may continue carefully through an intersection with a yellow light if:

options.text: There is an emergency vehicle crossing your lane.
There are pedestrians crossing.
You are turning right.
You are already within the intersection when the light changes to yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already within the intersection when the light changes to yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: You are driving and hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down. Don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Wait to make sure the emergency vehicle is not heading toward you.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Look for a train.
Be ready to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Slow down, look for trains, and be ready to stop. If lights flash or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Never go around the gate.

questions.question: You may drive across a dashed white line:

options.text: At any time.
Only during daylight hours.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross them when it is safe to change lanes.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign indicates:

options.text: That the speed limit is 20 mph.
The beginning of a reduced speed zone.
The increased possibility of encountering pedestrians.
The end of a reduced speed zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The end of a reduced speed zone.
questions.explanation: This sign marks the end of the school zone speed limit.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Maintain your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed without braking and carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for nearby traffic.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before entering the reduced speed zone.
You should reduce your speed to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: A "Reduced speed" sign tells drivers to reduce their speed. The new speed limit begins at the sign.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do?

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Accelerate quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After a school bus stops and opens its doors, watch for children walking along the side of the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into a driveway or to enter or exit a highway.

questions.question: When can you NOT cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is disabled.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if it is safe and does not interfere with other traffic.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers of your presence.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you time to react to problems ahead without emergency braking. This helps prevent drivers behind you from crashing into your vehicle.

questions.question: What do orange signs indicate?

options.text: Work zones.
Traffic rules.
School zones.
Directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zones.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers that people are working on or near the highway.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Honk your horn, steer left, and brake.
Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: First, honk your horn to get attention. If the other driver does not move, steer right. Do not steer left because if the other driver corrects, you may still crash. Brake firmly. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the impact.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Lane ends.
No right turn.
Slippery when wet.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow and black. This sign tells you that a lane is ending and you should prepare to allow traffic to merge safely.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when changing lanes?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Give a turn signal.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal. Check for other drivers moving into the same lane. Never use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.
Steep grade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead curves to the right and then to the left. Slow down to safely navigate these curves.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Do what other cars are doing, even if it goes against the guard's directions.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules for driving without children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Always follow directions from a crossing guard or police officer in a school zone. Slow down and use extra caution in these areas.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, a small vehicle driver must be ready for:

options.text: Loud noises.
Extra air pollution.
Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
Falling parts from the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles sideways. Be ready to steer to stay in your lane when passing large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn drivers you are entering.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert other drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly with traffic.
Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and all traffic on the roadway.

questions.question: What kinds of drugs can affect your driving?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold remedies
All of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: You should leave extra space when stopping:

options.text: On an incline.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On an incline.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your car when stopped on an uphill slope. This prevents a collision if the car ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Let other road users know what you are doing.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other road users know what you are doing.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Signal when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your horn when needed to alert other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You can never stop your vehicle there.
You can park there if you stay in the vehicle.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload goods.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you can only stop temporarily to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, safely move to the right side of the road and stop. In heavy traffic, move slowly to the side when you can. Clear the path for the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Construction workers on or near the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns that pedestrians may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly blocks the normal flow of traffic
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone
Only when driving in rural areas
When driving in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly blocks the normal flow of traffic
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you block the normal flow of traffic. You may get a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Reducing your ability to focus on driving
Decreasing your chances of an accident
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel
Making you more aware of others around you

questions.correctAnswerText: Reducing your ability to focus on driving
questions.explanation: Emotions affect your driving ability. If you are worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress reduces your concentration. It is better to wait before driving than to risk driving when you are emotionally upset.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn
Turn on your headlights
Reduce your speed
Check your mirrors and blind spots

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors to make sure no one is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: When a funeral procession is present, ____ has the right-of-way.

options.text: Another driver
A pedestrian
The funeral procession
A bicyclist

questions.correctAnswerText: The funeral procession
questions.explanation: All drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must let funeral processions pass. When the lead vehicle enters an intersection, the other vehicles in the procession can follow through, even if traffic signals say otherwise.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, which has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car approaching from the right
The car approaching from the left
The car whose driver sounds the horn first
The car traveling the fastest

questions.correctAnswerText: The car approaching from the right
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control device, you must yield to a vehicle coming from the right.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn
No turning
No left turn
No right turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits U-turns. Do not make a U-turn where you see this sign.

questions.question: You are stopped in a line of vehicles at a stop sign. If there is no cross traffic after the vehicles ahead pass through, you:

options.text: May go through the intersection without stopping again
Must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before going
May slowly roll past the stop sign
May follow the vehicle ahead without stopping

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before going
questions.explanation: You must always make a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not skip this step because other cars are behind you.

questions.question: A speed restriction sign:

options.text: Can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice
Has a triangular shape
Is blue with black lettering
Shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn

questions.correctAnswerText: Shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn
questions.explanation: Signs for curves and turns often show a recommended speed. Although you may feel safe driving faster in good weather, you should never drive at the posted speed in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Maintain
Vary
Reduce

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: When turning, reduce your speed to stay in control of your vehicle, keep in your lane, and react to unexpected situations.

questions.question: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, you may pass if:

options.text: Only in an emergency
You are on an expressway
Traffic is clear
Only at an intersection

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is clear
questions.explanation: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line with the broken line on your side, you may cross to pass if there is no oncoming traffic.
